tools.name: bf_catalogue
tools.description: Lists every Business Frameworks node: handle, title, layer, token count, price, whether it is free, and whether its decision rule can be run on numbers. Business Frameworks is operating judgement for running a business from launch to about $50M in revenue: value, cash flow, risk (the cost of capital

tools.name: bf_read_node
tools.description: Returns one node's text with its public citations, child handles, related handles and a cite-as line; `variant` chooses full (the default: lede, conditions, reasoning) or terse (the lede alone) at the same price. The free layer (the equation, the branch roots, value/15s and the decision-method nodes

tools.name: bf_decision_schema
tools.description: Returns the input schema, an example input and the price for one of the applied decisions (reinvest or distribute, build or run for cash, cash cycle, runway, owner pay, hurdle rate, concentration, pace of growth, price, adjacency; and, in the market branch, verdict, pricing power, binding node, rent

tools.name: bf_apply_decision
tools.description: Runs one decision node's rule on the numbers you send and returns the computed figures, a verdict, the actions in order, the check to keep and the node text with its citations. Deterministic: the result comes from the published rule, not from a model. Costs the decision's catalogue price ($0.05, USD

tools.name: bf_resolve
tools.description: Quotes the minimal set of nodes that answers a broad task — a decision bundle, a market (chain) bundle or a cross bundle — with its price, the sum of its nodes' catalogue prices, stated before anything is paid. Deterministic and free: a named bundle or decision wins, then the input fields sent, then

tools.name: bf_read_bundle
tools.description: Returns the nodes of one bundle in order — the central node full, the supporting nodes terse — with citations and a cite-as line per node, on one settlement at the quoted price (the sum of the nodes' catalogue prices, $0.05 to about $0.20, USDC on Base over x402). Pass the bundle id from bf_resolve

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: bf_read_bundle · Private data: bf_catalogue · Public sink: bf_apply_decision · Destructive: bf_catalogue, bf_read_node, bf_decision_schema.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: bf_read_bundle · Private data: bf_catalogue · Public sink: bf_apply_decision · Destructive: bf_catalogue, bf_read_node, bf_decision_schema

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
